title: Cloud Doctor: Session Log
subtitle: Every prompt, a summary of each response, and a timeline of the work
about: This log records each prompt you gave in this working session, in order, with a short summary of what was done in response. It is updated at the end of every turn.

Timing: the tool does not record a clock time per message. Entries are ordered by sequence number. The date shown is taken from the date the environment reported at that point, and is the container's date, so it may differ from your local date. No times are invented.

Prompts are quoted exactly as written. Automated messages (hook feedback, session notifications) are not prompts; they are noted inside the entry they belong to. The first prompt was a long hand-off summary produced by the previous session, so it is condensed and the standing rules in it are quoted.
Results are stated as measured. Anything not run is marked as not verified.

entries.title: Earlier session (summarised)
entries.prompt: Not available verbatim. The hand-off summary says the user was given the research challenge 'Cloud Doctor: Self-Healing Infrastructure' (Challenge 08).
response: Created the research plan (15 sections, 18 research questions) and the research map (26 domains, degraded-mode table, diagram tracker).
Locked in the core principle: deterministic systems own detection, policy, execution and verification; AI only advises.

Later work (before this session) froze the contracts (schemas, OpenAPI, database schema, telemetry contract), wrote ADRs, and built Stream A (plain-Docker sandbox) on branch stream/infra. Four cloud stream sessions (backend, policy, frontend, harness) were started.

entries.title: Hand-off prompt: act as coordinator
entries.prompt: [Continuing from a previous session] Summary for hand-off, then standing rules from the user: (1) never add Co-Authored-By lines or any Anthropic/Claude attribution to commits or PR text; (2) never name the user's previous company's product or its org, domain or mail-server names in generated documents; (3) Python backend plus Next.js/TypeScript frontend only, Go excluded (ADR-007); (4) report only measured results, unmeasured stays 'pending'; (5) small logical commits, one file per commit where practical, with detailed bodies; do not merge stream branches into main without explicit instruction. Deadline: build 31 Oct to 4 Nov 2026, MVP testing 5 Nov; full scope retained; AI phase last and nothing may depend on any LLM API. Coordinator role: (a) fetch and review stream branches; (b) keep sprint-status current; (c) prepare integration plan and gate scripts G2-G5 without merging; (d) Stream A remaining work only if Docker is available; (e) AI stream last.
response: Fetched the remote: only main, stream/infra and my branch existed; the four other stream branches had not been pushed.
Docker had no daemon in the cloud container; started dockerd as root. Image builds needed the environment's proxy certificate, supplied through a local override kept outside the repository.

make smoke passed with 17 checks. Added infra/tools/fault_worker.py and recorded one N=1 observation: killing the worker took up to 0 within about 3 s, processing stopped by about 9 s, and after restart the 855-job backlog drained in about 24 s.
Finding: queue_depth is exported by the worker, so it disappears while the worker is dead.
Added tests/integration/gate_g1.sh and a draft integration plan (gates G2-G5 marked pending).
Push failed with HTTP 403 (GitHub access missing); reported with the fix. A stop-hook reminder about unpushed commits arrived (automated); the retry failed the same way.

entries.title: GitHub reconnected
response: Push to stream/infra-p7f2rn succeeded; the branch was created on the remote with all commits.
Noted that sprint-status.md on main was still stale and needed the user's go-ahead to update on main.

entries.title: Check for all commits
response: Verified local and remote heads matched; listed my 5 commits on top of Stream A's 19.

A new branch, stream/backend, had appeared. Reviewed it in a throwaway worktree: contract validation passed, no contracts changed, 146 backend tests passed and 4 skipped, no LLM imports, no attribution lines in commits, and its STATUS.md claimed no measured results.
Flagged that its worker-crash fixture probably assumed a rising queue, contradicting the measured observation. Code itself was not read line by line.

entries.title: Finish pending work before laptop sync
entries.prompt: Finish any pending work and When I reconnect the laptop I'll sync the git repo
response: Confirmed the backend worker_crash fixture models queue_depth rising while the worker is dead, which contradicts the sandbox observation; recorded it as a mismatch to resolve before G2.
Tore down the sandbox, committed and pushed the note. Gave the laptop sync steps.

entries.title: Sync and check everything
entries.prompt: i'm online you can syn the files and check all things
response: Fetched all remotes: no new branches since the last check. Local matched remote; contract validation passed.
Listed what was still open: the three missing stream branches, sprint-status on main, and the backend fixture mismatch.

entries.title: Check all sessions, then sync them
entries.prompt: check all sessions then sync them
response: Listed the sessions: the backend, policy, frontend and harness sessions were all idle with finished work, but policy, frontend and harness had not pushed (likely hit the same GitHub 403).
Asked each of the three to push only its own branch; all three did, with matching hashes (two confirmed by message; the frontend branch was already on the remote).

Reviewed all four branches: contracts unchanged, no attribution lines, no Go. Reproduced results: backend 146, harness 134, frontend 132 tests; policy 317 passed plus 1 failed. The policy failure was intermittent (2 of 8 runs, a BrokenPipeError in an actuator server test).
Found that the Rego policy had never been executed, the Postgres audit sink was not started, and the harness had gaps (EXP-05, 11, 12 injection missing).
Collected the 10 contract change requests the streams filed. Wrote the review document with a table of all of this.

entries.title: Sync all branches locally
entries.prompt: ok first sync all repo branches to locally also
response: Created local tracking branches for all 7 remote branches in the cloud container, each at the remote commit.
Gave the commands to do the same on the laptop without touching checked-out work.

entries.title: How will the merge work, and in what order
entries.prompt: now how the merge will works like what will be order to be merged
response: Rehearsed all merges on a throwaway local branch (deleted afterwards): no conflicts, contracts unchanged, sprint-status unchanged.
Recommended order: infrastructure, policy, backend, harness, frontend, then the AI stream last (not yet existing).

Each suite passed on its own, but one combined pytest run gave 20 failures. Bisecting showed the cause: the backend switches from its local stub to the real invariants package once that package is importable.

Listed what to fix before merging: the backend vs real policy mismatch, the flaky policy test, the worker-crash fixture, the unexecuted Rego, and a decision on the contract change requests. Recommended merging into an integration branch first.

entries.title: Commit authorship objection
entries.prompt: you have commited with your username isn't i have specificcally told not to add your name or anything like that
response: Agreed and checked: my commit messages had no attribution lines, but the commits were authored and committed as Claude (noreply address). The same author was on the stream branches: backend 12, policy 4, frontend 7, harness 9 commits.
Also found and fixed a side effect of my own merge rehearsal: it had set the repository git identity to a placeholder.
Set the repository identity to the user's own name and email, and asked before rewriting history because it needs a force-push.

entries.title: Rewrite authors and force-push
entries.prompt: revert all commit author to my id and force push them
response: Saved local backup branches, then rewrote author and committer on every Claude-authored commit across the five pushed branches (8, 12, 4, 7 and 9 commits).
Verified before pushing: file contents identical to the originals, same commit counts, no Claude author left.
Force-pushed with a lease pinned to the old heads. main and stream/infra were untouched (already the user's).
Warned that the stream sessions still hold the old commits and should not push again without a reset.
artifacts: new heads: infra-p7f2rn 5462d6f, backend 01fefb0, policy faad7e5, frontend 956f6d1, harness 3baaa72

entries.title: Merge, after fixing what blocks it
entries.prompt: now i want to merge as you were saying before merging something need to be fix
response: Created the integration branch from main and merged all five streams: no conflicts. Nothing was merged into main.

Root cause of the 20 combined failures: the backend had only ever run against its own stub. With the real policy package every plan was denied (the backend passed its own catalogue type, no container labels, and misread an approved medium-risk plan). Fixed in the backend's policy adapter; the backend suite passes in both modes.
Fixed the flaky actuator test (a race in the test helper): 0 failures in 40 runs of the file and 8 full-suite runs, versus 2 of 8 before.
Made the worker-crash fixture model queue_depth as absent while the worker is down; updated two tests (RCA confidence is 0.65 instead of at least 0.7, one signal fewer).
Ran the Rego for the first time through the official OPA image (the vendor host is blocked): opa check exit 0, opa test 13/13 on OPA 1.22.0.

Verification: contracts pass; backend 146 (stub) and 131 (real, 19 skipped); invariants 129; actuator 83; policy 108; harness 134; frontend 132; combined run 585 passed, 0 failed. Pushed the integration branch.

entries.title: Apply the required contract changes first
entries.prompt: first do the required changes before merging them into main branch
response: Applied six of the ten contract change requests on the integration branch: policy-1 (A-* rule ids accepted), frontend-1 (report 404 documented), frontend-2 (API prefix stated), harness-2 (cause-id vocabulary published; two harness scenarios used ids the RCA never emits, fixed), harness-3 (approval semantics and audit event names documented), backend-1 (queue length exported by the probe sidecar).
Observed once on the sandbox (N=1): with the worker killed, the probe's queue length rose from 3 to 195 in 24 s while the worker's own queue_depth was absent.

Deferred with reasons recorded in each request: policy-2 (envelope attestations), frontend-3 (new endpoints), harness-4 (new collectors), and the backend's own use of the new queue metric. harness-1 needed no change.
Re-verified everything and pushed; asked whether to fast-forward main (not done).

entries.title: Are all branches merged into integration?

response: Checked each remote head against the integration branch: all six stream branch heads are included.
main was 84 commits behind and could be fast-forwarded; the AI stream does not exist yet (only a README). main was not changed.

entries.title: Complete harness-4 and map backend to frontend
entries.prompt: complete the harness 4 and map the backend to frontend
response: Harness-4: found CPU and memory were already exported. Added filesystem usage, client-side database call time, and database probe metrics (connections, limit, per-client counts, round-trip time), all in the telemetry contract. Observed once: holding 60 connections showed 60, attributed to the holding client, back to 0 on release.

Backend: new evidence and RCA rules for connection exhaustion (names the leaking client), network latency to the database (a slow database is not called network latency) and a full disk. New fixtures and tests: backend 151 passed (stub) and 136 passed with 19 skipped (real); harness 135 passed. The six affected scenarios moved from not recoverable to recoverable but unverified, because no run has observed the signals yet.

Found a design gap: at the connection limit the probe is locked out too, so counts vanish when they matter. Added a refusal flag so exhaustion is still evidenced. Not yet run on a sandbox: the rebuild hit a Docker Hub rate limit (HTTP 429).

Backend to frontend: wrote a live conformance check. Against the real backend and live sandbox: all 20 frontend calls exist in the contract, authentication and the idempotency rule are enforced, every endpoint that needs no incident validated against the schemas (0 failed). Seven incident-scoped operations were not exercised because holding 96 of 100 connections did not cause an incident (correct: the application kept working).
Work was interrupted by the user before the frontend was run against the real backend.

response: Explained that a session cannot be moved by me; stopped the backend and the sandbox so nothing runs in the cloud.
Committed all pending work in small commits and pushed the integration branch (d105ba0), authored as the user.

Added a hand-off section to the integration plan: what is verified, what is not (refusal flag never run, incident-scoped calls and the frontend against the real backend not exercised, new RCA rules only on synthetic data), what is open, and the exact next steps.
Noted that most cost came from repeated sandbox rebuilds and long test loops in the cloud container, and that running the unverified steps locally avoids the proxy and rate-limit problems.
